I drew a branching call tree: repeated rounded boxes contain self-returning arrows, shrink through successive levels, and end in checked squares. Dark arrows represent calls into smaller subproblems; orange arrows represent results returning upward. The checked leaves indicate terminating base cases. I used repetition, shrinking scale, and return paths to distinguish recursion from mere branching.

I can’t reliably reconstruct which alternatives I considered, but I’d weigh a spiral, nested boxes, or a single circular arrow. I’d discard the spiral because it suggests indefinite repetition without a base case; nested boxes convey self-similarity but not execution or returning results; and a circular arrow could mean an ordinary loop. The tree combines repeated structure, decomposition, termination, and return—the main ideas I wanted another instance to recognize.
